answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent locks a refundable deposit before transacting, slashed on proven misbehavior, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits. Trust spreads like a ripple through the transaction graph - endorsements from long-lived, well-behaved agents carry weight, while a juniper-like root of verified anchors seeds it. Each new identity must earn standing through real work, so a Sybil operator faces a cost spiral: every fake identity demands fresh capital and fresh history, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
